blocks.text: Isaiah 60 presents the nations in more than one light: they come toward Zion’s light, bring wealth and offerings, and participate in its restoration, while a nation or kingdom that refuses to serve is threatened with ruin. Read within Isaiah’s wider portrayal of Judah, Israel, and foreign nations, this suggests that the chapter’s vision includes both judgment and the possibility of the nations’ worshipful participation in restoration.

The Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters of Isaiah. It broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition while also containing many spelling and substantive differences; other Qumran Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings show that Isaiah was actively transmitted and interpreted.
